newsitem.title: RUSSIA: BMW considering car, engine production in Russia.
newsitem.headline: BMW considering car, engine production in Russia.

text.p: German automaker BMW AG said on Tuesday it was considering assembling cars in Russia.
"We are considering setting up a small factory on Russian territory to assemble cars for the Russian market," Wolfgang Vollath, BMW director for Russia, said at an automotive conference in Moscow.

"Duties levied on imports of ready-made cars into Russia are high," Vollath added. "A local assembly factory is a way for us to reduce costs while delivering the same quality cars...BMW is very much interested in working with a strong local partner."
He did not specify the type of cars the German automaker might build in Russia.

BMW, which owns British automaker Rover Group Ltd was also looking for a local partner to set up a local factory to produce Rover engines. "The Rover engines could be exported to other developing regions, too," he said.
Rover already supplies engines for Russian cars such as Okas made by AO AvtoVAZ and AO KamAZ and Volgas by AO Gorkovsky Avtomobilny Zavod (GAZ).

He said BMW also wanted to contract Russian suppliers for its projects, noting that there was "significant potential for local sourcing" of alloys, aluminium, ceramics, plastics, steel and other material.
"We have held discussions with GAZ about the purchase of machine tools," Vollath said.
